text:
JJ Peterka is on his third team in three seasons, and Boston is giving him the role he never quite held in Buffalo or Utah. He is playing 17:35 a night, up from 15:59, with 14 points in 20 games and a goal set up by David Pastrnak in the 4-1 win over Florida.

The underlying growth is the convincing part. His own chances are up to 1.15 expected goals per 60 from 0.73 last season (expected goals measure the quality of his shots), and the Bruins take 55.5% of the expected goals with him at five on five, better than without him. His skating shows up everywhere: 66 bursts over 20 mph, 96th percentile by NHL Edge.

If anything, the goals are behind. He has five on 6.7 expected, and he went seven games without one before the Florida game, though his teammates have finished well around him. Evolving-Hockey had him at replacement level last season while noting his chances deserved better. The test is whether his finishing catches up to his chances, or whether this is another season of good looks and few goals. Watch the next ten games.
headline: Peterka found more ice in Boston
